newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris mayor helped decide wife's fee - newspapers.
newsitem.headline: Paris mayor helped decide wife's fee - newspapers.

text.p: French newspapers said on Wednesday that Paris mayor Jean Tiberi helped fix a hefty fee for a report written by his wife which is now the focus of a corruption probe.

According to the investigative and satirical weekly Le Canard Enchaine, Xavier Dugoin, Gaullist president of the Essonne regional authority outside Paris, told a magistrate conducting the sleaze investigation, "The payment was negotiated between Mr Jean Tiberi and myself".
Tiberi's office said he was aware of the report but would have no immediate comment.

Le Monde said the word "negotiate" did not actually appear in the transcript of Dugoin's hearing before the magistrate but added that Dugoin did meet Tiberi several times to discuss the payment for his wife's report.

"I was able to talk to Jean Tiberi about the conditions in which I would resort to his wife's services," Dugoin was quoted by Le Monde as saying. "The payment of Mrs Tiberi was determined by myself in agreement with Jean Tiberi."

The allegation was a fresh embarrassment for the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) party of French President Jacques Chirac, which has found itself enmeshed in a series of recent sleaze probes involving senior party officials.
Both Dugoin and Xaviere Tiberi, the Paris mayor's wife, were formally placed under investigation last week on suspicion of misuse of public funds.
Investigators suspect Dugoin of paying 200,000 francs ($40,000) to Xaviere Tiberi for writing a 36-page report largely copied out of a book.

Dugoin's accusation appeared likely to drag the mayor himself into the probe. Tiberi was Chirac's deputy when Chirac served as Paris mayor, a post he held until he won the French presidency last year.

Gaullist Justice Minister Jacques Toubon has acknowledged ordering a helicopter chartered to track down a magistrate holidaying in Nepal in an effort to head off the probe of Mrs Tiberi, which was being pursued in the magistrate's absence by an independent-minded deputy.

Various other RPR officials including party personnel chief Louise-Yvonne Casetta are under investigation in unrelated probes into an alleged party fundraising scheme in which firms are suspected of having paid kickbacks to obtain Paris-area public works contracts.
